original_question: Find three perfect cubes whose product is a prescribed given number.
target_in_paper: Section 5.6, Problem 30: "Find three cubic numbers such that if the first is multiplied by the second, and the result by the third, the final product is a given number." ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
correct_elements: Your draft captures the right target almost exactly: it asks for exactly three cubic/perfect-cube quantities, and it keeps the defining condition that their product is a prescribed number. That is the substance of Section 5.6, Problem 30. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
missing_details: The paper's statement is a fixed-parameter existence/construction problem, so a stand-alone version should introduce the prescribed parameter explicitly (for example, N). ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

To be fully self-contained, the admissible number system must be specified. The paper as a whole is framed around integer or rational solutions, but Problem 30 itself does not locally say whether the three cubes are sought in integers, rationals, or some broader domain. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

A modern rewrite should say whether positivity is intended. In the historical arithmetic setting of the paper this is implicit, but it is not stated in Problem 30 itself. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

It should clarify whether the unknowns denote the cube numbers themselves or the underlying numbers whose cubes are sought; the paper's prose uses 'cubic numbers' and leaves that convention implicit. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))

No extra hypotheses such as distinctness of the three cubes, integrality of the prescribed number, or auxiliary side conditions are stated locally, so a faithful rewrite should not add them. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
refined_question: Given a prescribed positive rational number N, determine whether there exist positive rational numbers A, B, and C, each of which is a perfect cube, such that ABC = N; if such cubes exist, construct them. This is the closest modern stand-alone rendering of Section 5.6, Problem 30. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
justification: The draft clearly points to the multiplicative problem in Section 5.6 rather than to any neighboring cubic, quartic, or Diophantine problem. Its wording matches Problem 30 almost verbatim, so broadening it would be unfaithful. The only real deficiencies are modern expositional ones: the parameter is unnamed, the ambient solution domain is left implicit locally, positivity is unstated, and the variable convention is not formalized. The rewrite therefore stays exactly at Problem 30 and adds only the minimum clarifications needed to make it self-contained. ([ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org](https://ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html/2511.08400v1))
